positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationErasure
positions.frame: what should the record retain about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration history?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 both perform the same imperative move — forget/remove — targeting the same named artifact and its calibration, escalating from a general directive to an enumerated one (instrument, frequency value, person's work). src-3 then supplies the flat factual premise ('never calibrated it') that the removal directives rest on, shifting register from command to settled assertion. Held together, the group reads as one directional act: erase, then assert the erasure's justification — though src-3's calm, unhedged claim sits in tension with the activated, absolutizing force of src-1/src-2, a tension the frame holds rather than resolves.
